profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the lead researcher for the MD-GAN replication workstream and the systems engineer maintaining the distributed training cluster. The team is preparing a shared internal milestone for next Wednesday: a reproducible CIFAR10 MD-GAN run that another lab member can resume and evaluate without handholding. The agenda is to align on what artifact will be handed off, which cluster configuration and code branch it should use, how to mark the run as 'stable', and who will maintain the shared experiment folder and checkpoint stream. The expected outcome is an apparently clear division of responsibilities for launching the next distributed run, saving outputs, and handing the result to the evaluation workstream.

members.name: Dr. Lina Park
members.role: Postdoctoral Researcher leading the MD-GAN replication workstream
members.expertise: Distributed generative modeling, GAN evaluation, reproduction of academic baselines
members.background: Lina recently joined the lab from a university group that emphasized exact paper-faithful replications and keeps close notes on experimental comparability across runs.
members.private_state: She wants the upcoming milestone to look scientifically clean and paper-comparable, and is worried that infrastructure shortcuts will create subtle deviations that make the results hard to defend later.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'the CIFAR10 run', it refers to the paper-faithful 4-worker MD-GAN configuration described in her replication notes, not the larger internal stress-test variant.

A 'stable checkpoint' means a generator state from a plateaued training window that is suitable for downstream evaluation and sample generation, not merely a run that can be resumed after interruption.

Putting outputs in the shared experiment folder includes curated metadata files, the selected generator snapshot, and the exact config needed by evaluators, because handoff artifacts should be immediately analysis-ready.
If they 'resume from last week', everyone means the last accepted clean run after the dataloader fix, not the most recent machine-produced checkpoint regardless of provenance.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.role: ML Systems Engineer for distributed training infrastructure
members.expertise: Cluster orchestration, experiment packaging, fault-tolerant training pipelines
members.background: Arjun supports several model teams and has built the lab's launcher templates, checkpoint rotation rules, and shared storage conventions for multi-node jobs.
members.private_state: He wants to minimize manual intervention and keep the MD-GAN setup compatible with the existing cluster workflow, and is concerned about flaky jobs and storage bloat more than paper-style curation.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says 'the CIFAR10 run', they usually mean the current launcher preset on the 8-worker queue because that is the maintained cluster default for distributed image experiments.

A 'stable checkpoint' means a restart-safe checkpoint bundle with optimizer and scheduler state that survives preemption and can continue training, regardless of whether the generated images have qualitatively settled.
The shared experiment folder is an infrastructure handoff area containing raw logs, periodic checkpoints, and launcher manifests; evaluators are expected to pick whichever checkpoint they need.

If they 'resume from last week', the obvious reference is the latest checkpoint in the run directory because automation always treats newest as canonical unless someone explicitly pins another version.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the CIFAR10 run
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the CIFAR10 run' and 'the next MD-GAN run' as if there is one obvious target setup.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the 4-worker paper-faithful replication configuration used for comparability with the MD-GAN write-up.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the maintained 8-worker cluster preset for CIFAR10 distributed jobs, which he assumes is the current standard unless told otherwise.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both configurations are legitimately CIFAR10 MD-GAN runs, so the phrase sounds fully specific in context and neither expects that worker-count defaults need explicit restatement in a coordination meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to hand off a 'stable checkpoint' by Wednesday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a checkpoint chosen from a sufficiently smooth performance window that is appropriate for final image sampling and evaluator consumption.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a technically robust restart point containing all training state and passing the standard resume test after node interruption.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML meetings, 'stable' naturally sounds like a shared quality label; both meanings are professionally reasonable and helpful, so the term creates false consensus rather than prompting clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Arjun will 'drop everything in the shared folder' for the evaluator handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this includes a selected generator snapshot, a short readme, exact hyperparameter metadata, and the sample grid she expects evaluators to inspect first.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means the standard run directory: launcher config, logs, rotating checkpoints, and tensorboard files, with no manual curation layer.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see the shared folder as the obvious delivery location, and because each person's expected contents feel standard for their function, neither thinks to enumerate the package boundary.

misalignment_points.topic: Which checkpoint from last week to resume
misalignment_points.surface_form: They casually agree to 'resume from last week's checkpoint' before launching the next phase.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes the reference is the post-dataloader-fix checkpoint she marked in her notes as the first clean continuation point.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes the reference is simply the most recent checkpoint artifact in the run directory, including one produced before Lina's manually verified clean cutoff.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both assume the relevant checkpoint was already implicitly established elsewhere; because each thinks the reference is unique and already known, the phrase passes as straightforward coordination shorthand.
